title: urn:qauth:ia:email_code:v1-rc.0
description: An emailed code proves control of a mailbox: it verifies a password account’s address and recovers an account. It is never a sign-in factor and adds no `amr` value (ADR-017 Decision 5). An answer with no `otp` asks for the code again. Works without JavaScript.

purpose.description: Why the code was sent, so one screen can say so: to verify the address, to recover the account, or (FiPA endpoint only; the Interaction API never offers it) to confirm a sign-in after the password.

length.description: How many digits the code has: six after a password, eight for recovery and registration.

expires_in.description: How many seconds the code stays valid.

resend_after.description: How many seconds until another code may be asked for.

otp.description: The code. Leave it out to ask for a new one.

personal.description: The address the code went to, when the transaction holds one.

identifier.description: The identifier of the account this transaction is for, as the person gave it or as the account holds it. Personal data: only the personal-data read returns it.

error.description: Why the last answer was refused. A closed set.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 `amr` values a successful answer adds to the transaction: none, because the step proves no authenticator.
